newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends down, but trade support seen.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends down, but trade support seen.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended down on Tuesday but critically held above Monday's lows with help from trade buying.
May closed just off session lows, down 20 stg at 971 stg per tonne and July lost 21 to 987.
A weak morning saw a brief spike into positive ground then, when this failed to hold, traders expected fund selling to heat up again in New York and drag LIFFE down to test support at Monday's lows.
But when heavy sales failed to emerge at New York's open and support held, trade interest, speckled with light speculative buying, rippled into the market to bargain-hunt, traders said.
July cocoa resisted filling a gap between 982 and 985 on daily bar charts.
As prices drifted calmly in negative territory, switch activity reemerged, mostly in September/March and May/July as positions got rolled, traders said.

Though thoughts of about 21,000 open speculative May positions in New York before first notice day next week continued to weigh on prices, some traders saw the bargain-nibbling as a sign cocoa could form a base near current levels before moving higher again.
One trader pegged LIFFE May resistance at 1,000, with room in the near-term to test 1,020.

However, other traders were not yet convinced prices were ready to go higher. They said the market was only pausing after Monday's sharp drop. They expected the market to try again to fill the July gap before trying to turn up again.
Fundamentals did not justify a sharp cocoa rebound, they said, noting lower European grinds, recent rains that improved prospects for the Ivorian mid-crop and sterling strength.
Sterling reached a 4-1/2 year high against the mark early on Tuesday.
A healthy 12,046 contracts changed hands on Tuesday, with May grabbing 4,520 lots. July was second with 3,321 contracts and September with 1,076. --Medora Lee, London newsroom +44-171-542-8072
